strategy:
1. Approach and rationale
Use sequential trust-region linear-programming relaxations to generate feasible search directions, then minimize the exact finite-support minimax objective along each direction. This is materially different from projected log-sum-exp gradient continuation: it uses no smoothing, gradient, FFT, or SLSQP step. The original parent already has a nonsmooth minimax objective with bilinear terms; the LP replaces those terms locally with valid McCormick envelopes. A solved LP is only a direction generator, not a solution: recover its h-vector, perform an exact one-dimensional minimax search between it and the current feasible vector, and accept only a strict improvement under the evaluator’s exact score.

The justified facts are that each product h[i]h[j] has valid linear McCormick bounds on a box, so the resulting continuous LP is an outer relaxation of the corresponding trust-box problem; and along any affine segment each lag correlation is a quadratic, whose upper envelope can be minimized by checking endpoints, stationary points, and pairwise intersections. The hypothesis is that local product envelopes and diverse starts may expose useful directions near the supplied construction while exact acceptance avoids being misled by the relaxation. The method is heuristic for the full nonconvex problem: an LP lower bound need not yield an improving vector, local line searches do not establish a global optimum, and no score improvement is guaranteed. Preserve the validated parent as an incumbent and fallback.

2. Mathematical specification
For a runtime length n, use a float64 vector h of shape (n,), S=n/2, and dx=2/n. The feasible set is K={h: 0≤h[i]≤1 and sum(h)=S}. For each integer lag k from -(n-1) to n-1, define I_k={i: max(0,k)≤i≤min(n-1,n-1+k)} and j=i-k. Define Q_k(h)=sum over i in I_k of h[i](1-h[j]). The authoritative minimized objective is C(h)=dx times max_k Q_k(h), evaluated in the program as max(np.correlate(h,1-h,mode='full'))*dx. This includes all 2n-1 finite-support lags. In particular, nonzero lags use only their actual overlap; do not replace them with circular correlations or a full-mass autocorrelation identity.

In an LP trust box centered at a feasible vector x, with radius r, set l[i]=max(0,x[i]-r) and u[i]=min(1,x[i]+r). Introduce continuous variables v[i] for the candidate samples and z[i,j] for each unordered pair 0≤i≤j<n, representing v[i]v[j]. For each pair impose the McCormick inequalities
z[i,j] ≥ l[i]v[j]+l[j]v[i]-l[i]l[j],
z[i,j] ≥ u[i]v[j]+u[j]v[i]-u[i]u[j],
z[i,j] ≤ u[i]v[j]+l[j]v[i]-u[i]l[j],
z[i,j] ≤ l[i]v[j]+u[j]v[i]-l[i]u[j],
and l[i]l[j]≤z[i,j]≤u[i]u[j]. These are valid for all products in the box; for i=j the same inequalities give a valid diagonal relaxation, including the secant upper bound. For each lag impose sum over i in I_k of v[i]-z[min(i,j),max(i,j)] ≤ t, and impose sum(v)=S. Minimize t with bounds l[i]≤v[i]≤u[i] and 0≤t≤n. Every exact feasible sample vector and its exact products are admitted by this LP, so the optimum is a lower bound on the true trust-box minimax value. The extracted v and LP t are not an exact nonlinear solution; only an exact score check can accept v or a point on its line from x.

For a feasible line h(a)=x+a d, 0≤a≤1, with d=y-x and both endpoints in K, each lag is Q_k(h(a))=A_k a²+B_k a+D_k, where A_k=-sum over I_k of d[i]d[j], B_k=sum over I_k of d[i](1-x[j])-x[i]d[j], and D_k=sum over I_k of x[i](1-x[j]). The maximum of these quadratics on [0,1] attains its minimum at an endpoint, a stationary point of an active quadratic, or an intersection of two lag quadratics. Enumerate those candidates and compare their maximum-Q values; then score the selected line candidates using the exact np.correlate formula. The positive factor dx does not change the minimizing a.

Project any vector v jointly onto K using the Euclidean projection y[i]=clip(v[i]-lambda,0,1), where lambda is chosen so sum(y)=S. The sum is monotone in lambda, so bisection followed by residual redistribution gives a concrete box-and-mass feasibility operation; clipping followed by rescaling is not an acceptable substitute.

3. Implementation procedure
1. Define run(seed=42, **kwargs) at top level. Put every helper at top level and use no closures or lambdas. Use NumPy, scipy.optimize.linprog, and scipy.sparse.coo_matrix; use a local numpy.random.default_rng(seed) and keep all work serial for the one-CPU environment. Ignore unknown kwargs safely. Do not use filesystem or network I/O. The imported evaluate_erdos_solution may exist, but implement the exact score directly rather than depending on an external score estimate.
2. Read the pre-imported initial_h_values inside a guarded block without redefining or hard-coding it. Convert it to a local float64 copy. Accept it as a parent only if it is one-dimensional, has 2 through 999 entries, is finite, lies within [-1e-9,1+1e-9], and its sum is within 1e-6*max(1,n) of n/2. Clip only tolerated boundary roundoff, project it onto K, and pass the shared feasibility check. If accepted, derive n from its length and keep that projected vector unchanged as the fallback. If the global is unavailable or fails any check, use n=45 and the uniform feasible vector h[i]=0.5 as fallback. Do not resize or interpolate a valid parent.
3. Implement a feasibility checker for shape (n,), finite float64 entries, bounds within 1e-12, and mass error no more than 5e-12*max(1,n). Implement project_box_sum(v,S) as follows: reject non-1D or nonfinite input; set lo=min(v)-1 and hi=max(v); perform 80 bisection steps, setting mid=(lo+hi)/2 and y=clip(v-mid,0,1), moving lo upward if sum(y)>S and hi downward otherwise. Recompute y at the final midpoint. Let residual=S-sum(y); if positive, add it in index order by min(residual,1-y[i]); if negative, subtract it in index order by min(-residual,y[i]). Recompute the residual and make a final correction using coordinates with capacity in the required direction. Return failure if the remaining residual exceeds the feasibility tolerance or any bound check fails. This implements the projection onto the box and equality together.
4. Implement exact_score(h,n) to reject infeasible vectors with positive infinity, compute corr=np.correlate(h,1.0-h,mode='full'), and return float(max(corr)*(2.0/n)) only when the result is finite. The correlation length must be 2*n-1. Use this exact value for every start, line candidate, incumbent comparison, and returned score. Do not use the LP objective or a polynomial surrogate as the reported score.
5. Generate feasible starts algorithmically and project each through project_box_sum. With a valid parent and n≤64, use, in this order, the parent, its reversal, its complement 1-parent, np.roll(parent,n//3), parent plus projected centered Gaussian noise of amplitudes 0.04 and 0.12, and parent plus projected harmonic noise of amplitude 0.08. A harmonic noise vector is the sum of two cosines with seeded frequencies in 1..max(1,floor(n/2)), independent seeded phases and normal coefficients; subtract its mean and divide by its RMS, falling back to centered Gaussian noise if its RMS is below 1e-12. Circular roll is only a way to generate a start; always score the finite-support objective. For n from 65 through 96, use the parent, reversal, complement, and one projected seeded perturbation. Without a valid parent, start with the uniform vector, projected uniform-random and normal(mean=0.5, standard-deviation=0.25) vectors, and projected vectors 0.5+0.35*cos(2*pi*m*i/n+phase) for m=1 through min(3,floor(n/2)), with seeded phases. Deduplicate starts when their maximum coordinate difference is below 1e-10. Compute exact scores and update the global incumbent from every valid start before local optimization.
6. Implement a sparse LP builder for n≤96. Let P=n(n+1)/2, use variable order v[0:n], then P products, then t; the total variable count is n+P+1. For i≤j, the product index before the n offset is i*n-i*(i-1)/2+(j-i). Build the four McCormick rows and product bounds from the trust-box endpoints. For every k=-(n-1),...,n-1, loop i from max(0,k) to min(n-1,n-1+k), set j=i-k, and add coefficients +1 for v[i], -1 for z[min(i,j),max(i,j)], and -1 for t, with right-hand side zero. Add one equality row with coefficient 1 on every v[i] and right-hand side S. Set the linear objective coefficient of t to 1 and all other objective coefficients to 0. Use variable bounds [l[i],u[i]], [l[i]l[j],u[i]u[j]] for each product, and [0,n] for t. Assemble A_ub and A_eq as COO sparse matrices and convert to CSR; do not build a dense quadratic or lag-by-variable matrix. Call scipy.optimize.linprog with method='highs'. This is a continuous LP supported by that solver; no integrality or unsupported nonlinear constraint is involved. Catch solver exceptions and treat unsuccessful status or nonfinite/wrong-sized result.x as a failed proposal.
7. Implement line_minimax(x,y,n,S). Require feasible endpoints; set d=y-x. For all signed lags compute the A_k, B_k, D_k coefficients in section 2 using the actual partial-overlap index set. Build an alpha candidate list with 0 and 1, each in-range stationary point -B_k/(2*A_k), and every in-range real root of each pairwise difference (A_k-A_l)*a²+(B_k-B_l)*a+(D_k-D_l)=0. For a nearly linear difference solve the linear equation; for a quadratic use a stable quadratic formula, clamp a slightly negative discriminant to zero only within a scale-relative roundoff tolerance, and skip nonfinite roots. Ignore identical differences, clip roots only when they lie within a small 1e-10 tolerance of [0,1], then sort and deduplicate within 1e-10. Evaluate max_k(A_k*a²+B_k*a+D_k) for every candidate in vectorized chunks of at most 2048 alphas, so temporary storage remains bounded. Select the eight lowest predicted candidates, always also include 0 and 1, and include the best predicted alpha plus and minus 1e-8 when in range. For each distinct selected alpha, form x+a*d, pass it through project_box_sum to remove floating-point mass error, check feasibility, and score it with exact_score. Return the feasible candidate with the lowest exact score, breaking ties in favor of smaller movement. This enumeration finds the global minimum of the upper envelope along the segment in exact arithmetic; the exact-score filter protects against root and LP roundoff.
8. Implement local_lp_search(start,n,S). Project and validate the start, set current and its local exact-score incumbent to that vector, and set radius r=0.20. For at most eight LP attempts when n≤64 or five when 65≤n≤96, build and solve the trust-box LP centered at current. Before using result.x[:n], require all entries finite, within the trust bounds to tolerance 1e-7, and mass error at most 1e-7*max(1,n); clip only solver-sized trust-bound errors, then project onto the global K and validate. If this endpoint differs from current by less than 1e-12 in maximum norm, treat it as no improvement. Otherwise call line_minimax(current,endpoint,n,S). Accept a returned point only when its exact score is lower than current by more than 1e-12; on acceptance replace current, save its exact score, reset the consecutive-failure count, and set r=min(0.25,1.2*r). On failed LP, invalid output, or no exact improvement, keep current, halve r, and increment the failure count. Stop early when r<1e-3 and there have been at least two consecutive failures; otherwise stop at the attempt cap. Return the best exact-scored feasible point encountered, never the LP’s t or relaxed products.
9. For n≤64, run local_lp_search on every deduplicated start; for n from 65 through 96 use the four starts specified for that range. After each local search, update the global incumbent only for a feasible candidate whose exact score is lower by more than 1e-12. For n>96, do not build the quadratic-size LP. Score the fallback and at most five additional starts consisting of its reversal, complement, a roll, and projected perturbations. Then perform R=max(4,min(12,ceil(1200/n))) serial low-memory perturbation trials from the current global incumbent. Cycle amplitudes 0.005, 0.02, 0.06, and 0.12; alternate centered unit-RMS Gaussian and harmonic noise, project each proposal, and accept it as the incumbent only after a strict exact-score improvement. This bounded branch uses O(n) working vectors and retains the valid fallback if all proposals fail.
10. Before returning, project the global incumbent once more and check feasibility. Recompute exact_score on that exact vector. If projection, validation, or scoring fails, or if the repaired vector scores worse than the saved exact-scored fallback, select the fallback and recompute its exact score. No failed start or solver call may overwrite that fallback.

4. Search choices and useful variations
Use the defaults above: LP cutoff n=96, initial radius 0.20, radius growth 1.2 after exact improvement, halving after failure, radius cap 0.25, stopping radius 1e-3, and the stated LP-attempt and start limits. Use eight predicted line candidates plus endpoints and nearby alphas for exact checks. The cutoff avoids quadratic LP storage at the largest allowed parent lengths; the default n=45 uses the full LP method. All random starts and perturbations use the supplied seed.

A coder may use a cutoff between 64 and 128, an initial radius between 0.1 and 0.25, four to twelve exact-checked line candidates, and four to nine LP attempts per start, provided the sparse relaxation, signed-lag equations, exact acceptance, and fallback rules remain unchanged. These are in-program fixed settings, not values to discover by experiments. For n>96, retain the explicit low-memory branch rather than constructing a dense or unbounded quadratic model. Correctness requirements are the full finite-support evaluator, joint feasibility, exact scoring of accepted candidates, and retaining the parent fallback; none is a tuning choice.

5. Numerical robustness and memory use
For n≤96, the LP has n+n(n+1)/2+1 variables and 4*n(n+1)/2+2n-1 inequality rows. Build these rows sparsely; at n=45 this is about 1,081 variables and 4,229 inequalities, and even at n=96 it remains a bounded sparse LP. The line-envelope calculation has O((2n-1)^2) breakpoints in the worst case and evaluates them in chunks, avoiding a large candidate-by-lag temporary. Do not form a dense product tensor, Hessian, or lag-by-coordinate Jacobian. For n>96 use only O(n) candidate vectors and the bounded number of exact scoring calls specified above. Exact np.correlate scoring is O(n²) and is acceptable for these limits; all operations are serial.

Use float64. Reject nonfinite inputs, LP results, coefficients, roots, projected vectors, and scores. Subtract no terms from the evaluator to hide roundoff. Use a scale-relative tolerance for nearly linear root equations and discriminants, always retain the endpoints, and exact-score selected alphas. A HiGHS failure, infeasible numerical proposal, failed projection, or non-improving relaxation only shrinks the trust radius or skips that proposal. The projection’s bisection plus residual redistribution must preserve both box bounds and mass; if it cannot meet the feasibility tolerance, discard the vector. The global best is monotone under exact-score acceptance, and the valid fallback remains available even if every optimization step fails.

6. Runtime safeguards and return contract
The generated program must check the optional parent’s rank, length, finiteness, box range, and mass before using it; derive n from a validated parent and otherwise use n=45. Check feasibility before exact scoring and before every incumbent update. Compute the returned bound from the exact formula max(np.correlate(h,1.0-h,mode='full'))*(2.0/n) over all 2n-1 lags; do not report the LP value, a line-polynomial estimate, or a surrogate. If a solver or numerical stage fails, continue where possible and otherwise return the saved feasible parent, or the uniform vector when no parent was validated.

Implement the required top-level run(seed=42, **kwargs) and return exactly (h_values,c5_bound,n_points). h_values must be a float64 one-dimensional NumPy array of length n_points, every entry in [0,1], and its sum must equal n_points/2 to the projection tolerance. c5_bound must be recomputed from that same returned vector and be finite; n_points must be an integer from 2 through 999. Perform the final projection, validation, exact scoring, and fallback selection as program operations. Do not print, perform I/O, or claim an objective result before the harness executes the program.
